title: Customer-tailored eval modes with strict data boundaries
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers running Dedicated or Private deployments want continuous quality monitoring that is tightly coupled to model and configuration changes, but without any risk of sensitive prompt or customer data leaving their environment. Current eval scaffolding assumes centralized data and telemetry which is unacceptable for regulated customers.

Goal: Deliver a flexible "local-run" eval mode and per-customer eval profiles that: (1) can run inside customer networks (VPC or on-prem) with zero- data-egress, (2) provide reproducible, deterministic runs tied to a model/config manifest, (3) surface actionable deltas in Console/API and block or alert on regressions, and (4) support privacy-preserving telemetry (hashing/summary-only) for customers that allow limited aggregated signals.

Key capabilities:
- Per-customer eval profile: prompt/test set import, ground-truth labels, metric weights, and gating thresholds. Profiles stored in customer control plane (for Private) or tenant-isolated metadata for Dedicated.
- Local eval runner: lightweight container/binary customers deploy in their VPC/on-prem; pulls a signed eval manifest (model hash, config manifest, seed) and executes against pinned model artifacts or local model endpoints.
- No-egress mode: runner can be configured to never transmit raw prompts/responses. It emits only aggregated metrics and cryptographic hashes of inputs when permitted. An alternative run mode writes encrypted artifacts to customer-controlled object store (S3/GCS) for audit.
- Reproducibility: deterministic seed, fixed tokenizer/tokenizer versions, and a manifest that records model artifact checksum, quantization profile, and serving kernel hints so results correlate with the exact serving configuration.
- Rollout integration: Console + API support gating rules: block rollout if any weighted metric regresses beyond threshold or produce a canary failover. Automatic rollback hook to rollback rollout via the same config management flow.
- Privacy controls: per-profile toggle: full-cloud-run (for low-risk customers), summary-only telemetry (hash + metrics), or zero-everything (no telemetry; aggregated alerts only). Integrations with KMS/HSM for storing any secrets; runner can use customer KMS in Private mode.

Why this matters: This reduces adoption friction for regulated customers, enables our sales teams to confidently promise regression detection, and creates a repeatable path for surfacing and remediating quality issues tied to config/model changes without exposing customer data.

Constraints and trade-offs considered:
- Running evals in-customer increases compute footprint and support burden; we propose a small vetted binary with tight resource limits and clear troubleshooting docs.
- Full reproducibility may require shipping tokenizer binaries and quantization profiles; this increases artifact management complexity.
- Telemetry minimalism (hashes/summaries) reduces signal fidelity vs. centralized runs; we'll provide an opt-in richer mode for customers who consent.
acceptance_criteria: Console: create per-customer eval profile with prompt import, metric weights, and privacy mode selection
Local eval runner: deliver a container image + CLI that can run inside VPC with flags for: --no-egress, --summary-telemetry, --export-encrypted-artifacts
Manifest contract: signed eval-manifest format documented and supported by release tooling (model_checksum, config_manifest, tokenizer_version, seed)
API: endpoint to trigger evals and query latest eval results and gating decisions (returns pass/fail + metric deltas)
Gating: rollout pipeline honors profile thresholds and will block or mark canary failures when regression condition met
Privacy: support customer KMS reference and ensure no raw prompt text leaves customer boundary in no-egress mode
Telemetry: when summary-telemetry enabled, only metrics and deterministic hashes are sent; implementation reviewed by Security
Engineering: unit/integration tests validating deterministic runs across two identical runner runs (bitwise match for metric outputs)
comments: 2025-01-10 - Kickoff w/ENG (lead: Priya Rao) + Security + Solutions. Eng raised concerns about shipping tokenizer binaries. Agreed to support a compact tokenizer bundle per major model family (LLama-2, Mistral, etc.)

2025-01-16 - Design (lead: Jonah Kim) delivered initial Console mocks for 'Eval Profile' flow. UX focuses on privacy toggle with inline 'what it means' copy. Design review link: https://drive.redwood/example-eval-profiles (internal)

2025-01-22 - Eng spike completed: two implementation options explored: 1) Sidecar runner that calls local model endpoint; 2) Standalone runner that loads model artifacts. Sidecar preferred for Dedicated (faster), standalone required for air-gapped on-prem. Decision: implement sidecar first, standalone as follow-up.

2025-01-29 - Security review preliminary notes: require KMS integration, audit logging, and threat model for runner. Security requested a 'zero-evidence' mode where only HMAC'd digests are emitted. Marked security_review_required=true

2025-02-05 - PM sync w/ Sales: target pilot customers are 3 enterprise accounts with Dedicated + 2 on Private. Sales asked for SLA around eval-run latency (<= 2 hours for nightly runs) and guidance for compute sizing. Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-02-11 - Engineering PR opened for signed manifest format and runner bootstrap: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runner/pull/218 (internal). PR includes manifest schema and verification using our release signing key.

2025-02-14 - Scoped MVP: Console profile UI, runner basic binary with --no-egress and summary telemetry, rollout gating hook. Remaining work: standalone runner for air-gapped and encrypted artifact export flow. Estimate updated to 5 points.
